w:r.w:t: Sea of Okhotsk regional model validation
Sea of Okhotsk, LME_052. The selected model describes the whole sea.
Sea Around Us, 1950–2019 reconstructed catch. Reference: 2019 landings; all 151 exact reporting labels, including zero catch.
Chaikina (2004), A trophic mass-balance model of the Sea of Okhotsk for the 1980s period. BSc thesis, UBC, 49 pages. Original thesis unavailable. A related 2020 chapter documents the earlier model.
Radchenko (2015), Characterization of the Sea of Okhotsk Ecosystem Based on Ecosystem Modelling. A 48-group contemporary model is retained as an alternative; full reconstruction is unreviewed.

52_1_Sea_of_Okhotsk_NE_(1980). NE means newly constructed detailed Ecopath. It is a whole-sea 1980s annual-average model with 29 source groups and computational import 30. Reported area: 1,590,000 km².
Other models from the same article
The same source also compares a simplified nine-group SD 1980s model derived from the Shuntov–Dulepova food web. NE and SD are model structures, not northeastern and southern subregions.
Article — Retained as the broadest located whole-sea model despite incomplete original documentation.
Model — The detailed NE structure supplies finer biological resolution; existing numerical caveats remain.

Weights and assumptions: native group catches are unavailable. Canonical export=0 is not an observed stage fraction. Complete source biomass supplies every multi-group vector at Medium allocation confidence. Pollock supplies 48.9157% of 2019 landings and is allocated 53.874619% adult/nonjuvenile and 46.125381% juvenile, with equal catchability assumed and no recovered cutoff. Fixed 1980s proportions apply across all years and catch bases. Each rule table partitions the same simple-chain PPR.

Unresolved: Cyprinidae, because unobserved freshwater family composition supplies no defensible local marine home. It retains 177.054315 t landings and 1,241.263560 t C classic PPR in the denominator. Very low: 46 labels, 11.0196% landings and 4.1872% classic PPR. These include broad bony/invertebrate unions and unrepresented cartilage, pelagic and grazing-fish analogues. Source Salmon is mostly zooplanktivorous, limiting tuna/shark transfer. Failed TE has signed caught contributions; ordinary positive confidence percentages are unavailable.

R is the Sea Around Us Sea of Okhotsk LME. S is described by the source as the whole sea. The displayed polygon reconstructs that intended domain using R; author GIS and a study-area map are unavailable. Approximate A/B values therefore describe the intended proxy, not measured overlap.
Target LME 052 and intended whole sea proxy
WGS84 target area: 1,563,743 km². Source reported area: 1,590,000 km². Their area ratio is 98.3486% (target/source); it is not an overlap calculation. No geographic multiplier is applied.
